changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7125-dashboard-empty-state-keys-retired.md`

- names `DatasetWidget.tsx` → `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DatasetWidget.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `table.noRows` (`'No rows to display'`) and `engine.form.noRows` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, read at `widgets.tsx`) — two different, same-named keys in different namespaces. Nor the comments in `WidgetEmptyState.tsx`, `DatasetWidget.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and `PivotTable.tsx` that record WHY three widgets with three strings became one shared empty state; the packs' own comment keeps that rationale and now names the retirement instead of a row that is gone.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `4d0af04cb` (merge-base with origin/main): 4 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1622 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2211 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36343347941)

every `DashboardRenderer` caller in the tree (`packages/app-shell/src/views/DashboardView.tsx` fed by `AppContent`'s route, `metadata-admin/previews/DashboardPreview.tsx`, `DashboardWithConfig.tsx`, `apps/site/app/components/SchemaThumbnail.tsx`, and the `dashboard` registration in `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/index.tsx`); PR objectui#10809 (`8c3d7fc`): its `ObjectDataTable.tsx` hunk and `ObjectDataTable.invalidationRefetch-10778.test.tsx`; the `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` CHANGELOG entry that made the no-adapter alert deliberate ("A dataset-bound widget arriving with NO data source renders a visible state, never a blank … routing through it unconditionally cures both halves with one diagnostic and one wording"); objectui `AGENTS.md` §5 #8 and #11, §9 (怎么跑测试, 测试纪律, 版本号策略, the changeset-presence rule); `.changeset/config.json` (`fixed` group holds `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`); the pending `.changeset/7125-dashboard-empty-state-keys-retired.md` and `.changeset/dashboard-widget-dataset-stale-cast-5067.md` (the only pending changesets naming a touched file); `packages/components/src/custom/refresh-indicator.tsx` (`if (!active) return null`), `packages/components/src/lib/utils.tsx` (`cn` = `twMerge(clsx(inputs))`); `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` (`dashboard.refreshing` present in the `dashboard` block); `packages/plugin-dashboard/package.json` (deps / devDeps), `tsconfig.test.json`, the root `vitest.config.mts` alias map; `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts` `queryDataset` (`object` derived as `typeof data.object === 'string' ? … : undefined`, returned in the envelope); the three idle-markup metric pins (`DatasetWidget.colorVariant`, `.subCaption`, `.unrenderedMeasures-8894`, all `container.innerHTML` byte equality); the head's check-runs from the API, twice; one run of the two new pin files in my own detached worktree of `4fd37c1` under `os-verify-lock.sh` (slot `review-10837`).

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The adapter resolution — RIGHT.** `useResolvedDataSource(explicit)` is, verbatim at the head: `const named = isElementDataSourceConfig(explicit) ? undefined : explicit; return (named ?? context?.dataSource ?? undefined)`, reading `React.useContext(SchemaRendererContext)` directly (no throw without a provider, unlike `useSchemaContext`). So: explicit prop first, provider context second; a spec BINDING handed under the name `dataSource` (a plain object with a non-empty string `object` and no `find` function, per `isElementDataSourceConfig`) is discarded and the context is read instead. On BASE the renderer destructured `dataSource` from props and handed the raw value on. Behaviour change for a caller passing a non-adapter value: a binding object or `null` used to reach `DatasetWidget` and paint the alert; at the head it falls through to the provider's adapter. No in-tree caller does either: `DashboardView` gets `dataSource` from `AppContent`'s route (`‹DashboardView dataSource={dataSource} /›`), `DashboardPreview` passes `adapter as any`, `SchemaThumbnail` hands the gallery source both as context and as prop, and `DashboardWithConfig` passes no prop, so it now takes the ambient adapter (the PR body says so). This is the same rule `object-grid`, `object-form` and `detail-view` already apply. The page path: `SchemaRenderer` strips the node's `dataSource` key (`dataSource: _dataSource` in its destructuring, with the objectstack#5576 comment) and injects no adapter prop — the only `dataSource` a component receives is an explicit React prop via `...props` — so on BASE a `dashboard` block on a page had `undefined`; at the head it resolves to the context. Every child is fed the one resolved `const dataSource` (the prop is renamed `dataSourceProp`, so `...props` cannot leak the original): the self-contained arm's `SchemaRenderer schema={componentSchema} … dataSource={dataSource}`, the Card arm's `DatasetWidget … dataSource={dataSource}` and its `SchemaRenderer` twin, and `DashboardFilterBar … dataSource={dataSource}` (whose `SelectFilter` reads `def.optionsFrom` against `dataSource.find` / `dataSource.queryDataset`). `DatasetWidget` passes its own `dataSource` prop on to `DrillDownDrawer`, so the drill drawers get the same adapter transitively. An explicit prop still wins (`named ??` short-circuits), pinned twice: directly on `DashboardRenderer` and handed through `SchemaRenderer`, with `expect(ambient.queryDataset).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`.

**2. The no-adapter alert — RIGHT.** No provider: `context` is null, the prop is undefined, the hook returns `undefined`; `DatasetWidget`'s effect hits `if (!src || typeof src.queryDataset !== 'function')` and sets `dashboard.datasetUnsupported` — the CHANGELOG's deliberate state, untouched by the diff. A provider binding `null`: `undefined ?? null ?? undefined` → `undefined` → same alert. A context adapter without `queryDataset` (`{ find }`): resolved to that object, fails the `typeof src.queryDataset !== 'function'` test → same alert. All three are pinned as controls (`getAllByText(UNSUPPORTED)` length 3, inside `[role="alert"]`), and each is green on BASE by construction, since BASE also handed `undefined` on those paths.

**3. The bus reader — RIGHT, with one boundary note.** The effect's dependency list is now `[signature, invalidationNonce]` where `invalidationNonce = useDataInvalidation(…)` is handed `datasetObject` when `values.length` is above 0 and `undefined` otherwise — the same hook and the same `dataChangeMatches` matcher PR objectui#10809 put in `ObjectDataTable` / `ObjectPivotTable`; no second channel, no `key=` bump anywhere in the diff. The key is the dataset's base object as the ANSWER names it (`res.object`), kept in its own `useState` (`datasetObject`), set only inside the `.then` after the `if (cancelled) return` guard. The dev's claim about `state.object` is verified against BASE: every read wrote `setState({ status: 'loading', rows: [] })` and every error `setState({ status: 'error', rows: [], error })`, both dropping `object`, so it could not carry a subscription. At the head a failed re-read writes the error state but never touches `datasetObject`, so the subscription survives; the next nonce re-runs the effect (from the skeleton, since `prev.status` is `'error'`). A query change moves `signature`, the effect re-reads, and the answer's `object` replaces the key. Before the first answer lands `datasetObject` is `undefined`, so `useDataInvalidation(undefined)` subscribes to nothing (its own `if (!objectName) return`): a bus event during the first in-flight read is not observed, which is exactly `ObjectChart`'s dataset arm. Boundary note (③): `setDatasetObject` is called only when the answer names an object, whereas `ObjectChart` writes `res.object ? res.object : undefined`; after a rebind to a dataset whose answer omits `object`, the old key is kept. Consequence is an extra re-read on the old object's writes, not a missed refresh (`'*'` still matches), and the real adapter names `object` whenever the server does.

**4. In-place re-read — RIGHT.** The loading write is now a functional `setState` updater: when `prev.status === 'ok' && prev.signature === signature` it returns `{ ...prev, refreshing: true }`, otherwise `{ status: 'loading', rows: [] }`; and every `ok` write carries `signature` from the effect's closure. Same query: rows stay, `refreshing: true`, the `refreshBar` (`RefreshIndicator active={!!state.refreshing}`) mounts as a positional sibling ahead of the export button / table, so the `‹table›` node is reconciled in place — pinned by `toBe(table)` on the same node before, during (`hold()`) and after the re-read, and `queryByTestId('dataset-loading')` null during it. Changed query: `prev.signature !== signature` → `{ status: 'loading', rows: [] }` → the skeleton branch (`state.status === 'loading' || 'idle'`); the old rows cannot be shown under the new signature because the only `ok` state that carries the new `signature` is written from the new answer. A late answer for an older run: each effect run owns a `cancelled` flag set by its cleanup, both `setState` and `setDatasetObject` sit behind `if (cancelled) return`, so a superseded run (by signature or by nonce) writes nothing. Metric tile idle markup: `cn('flex h-full w-full flex-col items-start justify-center gap-1 p-2', state.refreshing && 'relative')` — `clsx` drops `false`, `twMerge` of the unchanged string returns it unchanged — and `RefreshIndicator` returns `null` when inactive, so the idle `container.innerHTML` the three pins compare byte-for-byte is unchanged. Table / matrix / chart roots already carried `relative`.

**5. Pins — RIGHT.** Both files render through the real `SchemaRenderer` under `SchemaRendererProvider` with `import './index'` registering `dashboard` and no host prop unless the case is about one. `ambientSource`: (a) `waitFor(datasetCalls(ambient)).toBe(3)` plus the painted `Won` inside a `‹table›` and the metric `7` — on BASE the renderer hands `undefined`, zero `queryDataset` calls, so this fails (`expected +0 to be 3` is what the assertion yields); (c) three controls green on BASE and head; (d) explicit prop wins, direct and through `SchemaRenderer`. `invalidationRefetch`: a bare `useDataInvalidation('deal')` reader (`BusControl`) is the lit control in every case; `'*'` → 2 reads, same table node; own object → 2 reads after an unrelated object left it at 1; the held re-read keeps the rows under `refresh-indicator` with no skeleton; `dashboard-grid` with a host prop re-reads (on BASE `DatasetWidget` names no nonce → 1 read → fails); the `{ find }` adapter subscribes to nothing and keeps the alert. On BASE the page-path bus cases fail at `findByText('Won')` because nothing loads. No `.skip` / `.only` / `timeout` / `setConfig` / `vi.mock` in either file (scanned); the only waits are RTL defaults and a 150 ms `settle()`. Side-effect imports are at module scope per 测试纪律. `@object-ui/plugin-charts` is a declared devDependency of the package.
